Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors: Anxiety symptoms for ~2 months with morning fear about leaving home; sleep disturbance (difficulty falling/staying asleep; ~3–4 hours on poor nights); daytime fatigue and anhedonia; palpitations described as irregular and occasionally alarming; social withdrawal and reduced activity; potential work-related stressor (new job and perceived poor support). No chronic diseases documented in the chart. Noted lifestyle factors include weekend alcohol use; occasional smoking; strong support system (family at home).

- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Lives with parents; mother has history of depression.

- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Not recorded.

- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.

- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.

- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Recently reduced exercise (ran/played tennis in the past; currently not engaging in these activities); regular meals reported; alcohol use predominantly on Friday/Saturday with occasional weekday intake; tobacco use intermittent but not regular; open to non-pharmacologic strategies and therapy.

- Hearing and vision concerns: Not recorded.

- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Distressed with persistent anxiety, low mood, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, and social withdrawal; no suicidal ideation reported; supportive family available; willingness to pursue talking therapy; no current plan for self-harm.

- Social context: Lives with parents; strong family support; perceives workplace stress as a primary trigger; no acute housing or financial crises noted.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (High likelihood)

  - Rationale: Onset within ~2 months after starting a new, stressful job; persistent excessive worry centered on work performance; significant sleep disruption and daytime impairment; avoidance of social/ recreational activities; mood symptoms including low energy and anhedonia.

- Supporting differential diagnoses (per DDx, with context from transcript)

  - Major Depressive Disorder with anxious distress (Medium): Persistent low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, and sleep disturbance present alongside anxiety features; duration ~2 months with functional impairment. Not enough detail to confirm full MDD criteria without additional symptom breadth; still plausible comorbidity.

  - Generalized Anxiety Disorder (Medium): Chronic excessive worry across multiple domains with autonomic arousal (racing heart) and sleep disturbance; duration emerging over ~2 months; may evolve toward GAD with time.

  - Hyperthyroidism (Low): Palpitations and anxiety could reflect thyroid dysfunction; not evidenced by symptoms beyond anxiety/palpitations; thyroid testing would help rule in/out.

- Considerations: If symptoms persist or worsen, evaluate for comorbid depressive disorder or other anxiety spectrum disorders; assess thyroid function and basic metabolic panel to exclude medical mimics; consider screen for caffeine or stimulant use contributing to anxiety/palpitations; assess alcohol use impact on sleep and mood.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Provide sleep hygiene guidance; discuss stress management strategies; encourage gradual re-engagement in physical activity as tolerated; provide information on self-management resources for anxiety.

- Patient health goals and priorities: Reduce anxiety to improve sleep and daytime functioning; restore engagement in activities; establish routine work-life balance; pursue appropriate mental health therapy.

- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.

- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Referral to mental health services for one-to-one therapy; self-refer via NHS (provided link); offer online resources; consider social supports as needed.

- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Follow-up with GP in 1 week after laboratory testing to review results and refine plan; continue to monitor mood, anxiety, sleep, and functional status.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Recommend one-to-one therapy; provide self-referral option and immediate online resources.

- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not indicated at this time.

- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not indicated.

- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not indicated.

- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not indicated.

- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not indicated at this time.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Onset soon after a significant life stressor (new, demanding job); persistent work-related anxiety with sleep disturbance and functional impairment; behavioral avoidance and mood disturbance consistent with adjustment reactions.

- Major Depressive Disorder with anxious distress
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Persistent low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, and sleep disruption present for ~2 months; anxious distress present; however full depressive symptom criteria and duration require further assessment.

- Generalized Anxiety Disorder
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Ongoing excessive worry with autonomic arousal (racing heart) and sleep disturbance; duration ~2 months; may evolve toward generalized anxiety if symptoms persist.

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs not recorded; no immunisation review documented; no objective body measurements (BMI/waist) recorded; no laboratory results available in this note.

- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None identified; DDx aligns with symptoms described (anxiety, sleep disturbance, mood changes) and the patient’s narrative of work-related stress.

- Transcript quality notes: Not recorded. The patient reports subjective palpitations and episodic chest discomfort; no objective findings available in the transcript.
